RECOMMENDATION FROM THE FACULTY SENATE EXECUTIVE COMMITTEE CHANGES TO 2020-2021 UNIVERSITY MANUAL APPENDIX C: BY-LAWS OF THE FACULTY SENATE: Section 7.
Quorum and Meeting Times. 7.1 A majority of the elected Senate shall constitute a quorum except at special meetings where there shall be no quorum required if actions taken at such special meetings are to be returned to the Senate for final action. 7.2 Regular Senate meetings shall begin at 3:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as a quorum is determined to be present, and shall be adjourned at 5:00 p.m.
When the Senate fails to complete its agenda within the time limit, the meeting either (1) shall be recessed and reconvened one week thereafter at the usual time, or (2) shall be adjourned and the unfinished business postponed definitely until the next regular meeting of the Senate. 7.3 Regular Faculty Senate Meetings shall be held at least once each month on Thursdays during the academic year. #00-01–28 7.4 At all Senate meetings debate on each main motion, each amendment thereto and discussion subsequent to informational reports shall be limited to fifteen minutes.

Debate may be extended in any Senate meeting by one-third vote of the members present. 7.5 In the event that Senate meetings are held virtually, Senate meetings may extend past the 5:00 p.m. required adjournment time (see 7.2) for a period of no longer than 30 minutes.
Virtual meetings may not extend past 5:30 p.m.
At 5:00 p.m. a motion to extend the meeting must be called and passed.
If discussion is not completed in fifteen minutes, one more motion to extend the meeting must be called and passed.
When the Senate fails to complete its agenda in the virtual meeting within the time limit, the meeting either (1) shall be recessed and reconvened one week thereafter at the usual time, or (2) shall be adjourned and the unfinished business postponed definitely until the next regular meeting of the Senate. 1

1 FACULTY SENATE OFFICE UNIVERSITY OF RHODE ISLAND FACULTY SENATE September 17, 2020 Faculty Senate Curriculum and Standards Committee Report 2019-2020-12 At the July 28, 2020 special summer meeting of the Curriculum and Standards Committee, the following matters were considered and are now presented to the Faculty Senate. SECTION I Informational Matters NEW TEMPORARY (X) COURSES: COLLEGE OF ENGINEERING: EGR 101X, Engineering's Response to COVID-19 (1 cr.) Invited speakers discuss how the engineering profession has and is responding to the coronavirus pandemic. (Seminar 1) S/U only. ELE 446X, Introduction to Power Electronics (3 crs.) Principles of power electronics: switched-mode converters; AC modeling; controller and compensator design; magnetic circuit theory. Examples such as server and network power supplies, grid-connected power systems, and wireless power transfer. (Lec. 3) Pre: ((ELE 212 or 220 or OCE 206) and PHY204 and MTH (244 or 362)) or permission of instructor. Not for graduate credit. COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES: GEO 101X, Undergraduate Seminar: Hot Topics in Geosciences (1 cr.) Seminar featuring oral presentations of the results of current topical research with individual student investigations. Compressed model yields 1 credit for 4 weeks of work. (Seminar) Pre: Any 100-level course in GEO, NRS, OCG, BIO, CHM, PHY. May be repeated for a maximum of 4 credits with a different topic. COLLEGE OF ARTS AND SCIENCES: AAF 120X, Rewatching The Watchmen: Race and Media (1 cr.) Revisits The Watchmen graphic novel and HBO series to consider African-American history, the intersection of race and gender, the landscape of new media, and pop-culture's role in inspiring social change. (Online) S/U grades only.

2 AAF 207X, Conversations on Race (1 cr.) Examines American conversations about race.
Students survey current attitudes on race in popular culture, internet, social media and major networks and then host an online forum on race. (Online) S/U grades only.
CCJ 100X, Interrogating Criminal Justice Reform (1 cr.) Overview and analysis of selected topics essential to criminal justice reform agendas.
Topics focus on the criminal justice system’s role as a social institution and mechanism of social stratification. (Online) S/U grades only.
ENG 150X, Tolkien, Wordsworth, and Escapism (1 cr.) Consideration of the political, intellectual, and aesthetic qualities of escapism as a practice of self care and engagement in challenging times, through the work of two master practitioners of the concept: Wordsworth and Tolkien. (Online) S/U grades only.
HIS/APG 392X, The URI Campus: A Walk Through Time (1 cr.) Exploration of the complexities of place and power through time.
URI was founded in 1892, but the history of this space is much older and intertwined with the Narragansett People. (Online) S/U grades only..

PSC 101X, Workplace Readiness for Social Science Majors (1 cr.) An online career readiness workshop designed for social science majors in the College of Arts and Sciences.
Students create personalized content and discuss various related topics with associated URI alumni. (Online) Pre: sophomore, junior or senior standing; for CCJ, AAF, SOC, APG, ECN, GWS, or PSC majors only.
S/U grades only.
PSC/AAF 301X, Racial Inequality in Government and Politics (1 cr.) Introduction to anti-racist theory and the cultural and societal implications of the manifestation of racism in institutions, culture, and most critically, government policy. (Online) S/U grades only.
SCM 351X, 2020TV: Broadcasting Contemporary Issues (1 cr.) Examination of the realities of 2020 with students producing content responding to current issues and topics concerning contemporary challenges for a weekly web broadcast, shot and captured remotely with Zoom. (Online) S/U grades only.
SOC/APG 140X, Anti-Black Racism and White Supremacy (1 cr.) Examine key causes and consequences of anti-black racism and white supremacy in the United States.
Reflect and engage with a learning community on these issues. (Online) S/U grades only.

FSEC (Faculty Senate Executive Committee) Meeting Minutes Date: Wednesday, September 17, 2025 - Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 noon Pastore Hall, Room 224 Remote option via ZOOM Action Items: Staff will post the Acronym Glossary on the FS webpage.
Committee liaisons need to be sure drafts of proposed legislation are taken up by appropriate review committees in a timely fashion.
FSEC members should be prepared to make suggestions for the remaining Joint Committee open seats on 9/24.
FS Pres. and staff will develop a calendar of “guest appearances” at FSEC weekly meetings for the remainder of fall semester.
The Coordinator and Specialist will assign appropriate Kuali access to the student CASC representative. 1.
Call to Order - FS President Williams called the meeting to order at 10:01.
VP Preisser and Sens.
Daniels, Meenach, Trimm and Van Wyk were present. 2.
Minutes - Minutes of the 9/10/25 meeting were tabled. 3.
Priority Items 3.1 Sept. 11 Senate Orientation - Re-cap - It was generally agreed that the event went very well.

Some key points to stress on 9/18 include the necessity for remote attendees to log in using a URI account, and the logistics of transitioning away from using the term “report” when addressing proposed legislation (“bills”).
It was also noted that not all senators attended and this is especially concerning where newly elected members are concerned.
It was noted that some legitimate scheduling conflicts are being encountered, some of which are unavoidable given the timing of elections in relation to setting course schedules, etc.
Lack of familiarity with senate jargon becomes evident in conversations with new members, and staff was asked to put the FSEC’s “acronym glossary” on the FS website as a resource for all. 3.2 Meeting planning - Sept. 18 FS Meeting - see agenda - the agenda was discussed and key FSEC in-meeting duties were addressed.
FS Pres.
Williams will note during the meeting that a move away from the “Consent Agenda” is desired, and unless the senate finds itself struggling to complete business in the time allowed, this tool may not be used this year.
Staff will assist with assembling a brief slide deck regarding the four new initiatives under Item 6.

The University President will offer a report, including a budget presentation. 3.2.1 Finalize travel path for introduced legislation - All four items under Item 6 on the agenda (c - f) will require CBUM review.
Some projects, like the streamlining initiative, will require endorsements from entities outside the senate committee structure (college curriculum chairs, for example).
The OIGE has already been consulted on the Gen Ed “partials” proposal and TAAC will be asked to review and comment on the SGO-related initiatives.
The Honors Program is prepared to endorse the “graduating with distinction” proposal at the 9/18 meeting. 4.
Continued Items 4.1.
Faculty Concerns submitted through the FS Webpage - No new concerns. 4.2.
Committee Assignment Updates - Finalize Joint Committees - Specific vacancies were discussed and some appointments were finalized.
A COB representative to JAPROA is still needed along with two faculty member representatives each on the IPC and University Conduct Board.
The CASC and GEC Chairs need to assign a member as liaison to JCODL. 1

Pres.
Williams will correspond with those Chairs about this need.
FSEC members were asked to be prepared to make suggestions for the remaining seats on 9/24. 4.3.
Reviving work of restructured JCODL - No new report. 5.
New Items 5.1.
Develop a visitor schedule for fall FSEC meetings - suggestions for special visits include the AVP of Facilities Karl Calvo; AVP Adams regarding the NECHE accreditation review; various standing and joint committee chairs - JCSC Chair Reyes might be especially timely; a discussion with Interim Dean Mouw re: the external review of the Graduate School.
Other suggestions included Dean Libutti re: URI Cares; AVP Lavan re: JCODL and JAPROA; AAUP representatives to discuss the national AAUP report on AI; Ray Wang, the new Library Interim Dean; and CIO Fariello as the university moves toward adoption of sweeping IT policy updates. 5.2. “Weaponization” of overlap concern in newly proposed courses - A complaint about a CASC approval delay related to perceived overlap concerns was discussed and several points were made in response.
First, it was noted that proposers in Kuali must not confuse a CASC “table” or "send back” with a rejection.

These steps are often taken when a relatively straightforward piece of additional supporting documentation is needed, and it does not generally presage rejection of a proposal.
Second, proposal quality matters and “overlap statements” must be thorough and substantiated.
Third, the CASC review is too late in the approval process for overlap concerns to be meaningfully addressed.
CASC has consistently and systematically tried to push this issue “down the chain” to the college and department curriculum committees where it can be better grappled with.
The overlap discussion highlighted for FSEC members the need for faculty to be trained in the curriculum process.
Most “information” shared in the departments about initiating proposals is simply “lore” passed down by word of mouth.
The online resources available tend to focus on the technical aspects of Kuali rather than on best practices in creating curricular proposals.
More standardized guidance is probably needed. 5.3.
How Honors sections get approved - a concern was raised to FSEC by a faculty member about a lack of vetting for H-section courses (“H” suffix courses, not HPR courses).

FSEC agreed they did not have enough information or examples to assemble a response and will need to circle back to the source before taking up the issue again. 5.4.
Student access to Kuali - the Student Senate has not had a CASC representative in recent years but does have a member willing to serve this year.
In order to contribute to committee work, access to Kuali would be required.
Kuali use is otherwise reserved for faculty and select administrators.
Staff will explore technological options, granting either “view only” access or access at the lowest permissions level as appropriate.
Pres.
Williams will also have an informal conversation with the student about the norms of confidentiality and circumspection in committee work. 6.
Updates 6.1.
Updates (meetings with administrators, other committee meetings) 6.1.1 Policy Reviews - APC met 9/16 - The agenda included the Research Misconduct Policy and the Conflict of Interest and Commitment Policy, both of which were approved. 2

The Conflict of Interest and Commitment Policy draft had contained complicated language about Honoraria which was stricken.
The VPAF’s team will subsequently work toward developing a set of procedures to address concerns about honoraria.
A policy related to course material adoption has been tagged for development this year.
FS Pres.
Williams plans to assert the Faculty Senate’s full purview in development of this policy.
In terms of other updates, Pres.
Williams noted he has requested a meeting with CIO Fariello to talk about issues like the university’s relationship to the Google “universe” and if/how/when it might detangle from it, and faculty concerns around administrator permissions in computing, among other things.
He has also corresponded with ITS about Brightspace concerns and has asked for advance notice to Senate leadership and more nuanced messaging around such tech changes/updates.
A brief update on the Centers/Institutes restructuring work was also provided.
A re-worked draft will be shared with FSEC when the document has been edited. 6.2 FOIA/APRA training for faculty - no update. 7.
New Business – Open for additional items not listed in the agenda.
Sen.

Trimm asked about the status of the mutual defense compact that the faculty senate acted on last spring and other efforts to coordinate with public New England institutions in response to federal actions and other threats.
Pres.
Williams noted that various leadership changes and other variables led to a “quiet summer” in this regard and it is as yet unclear if coordinated activities will ramp up again in AY 2025-2026.
Sen.
Trimm noted that, in the meantime, the AAUP has promoted some initiatives aimed at networking campuses across the country and this includes a “sanctuary campus network” that is focused on dealing with ICE activity.
More information is available for those interested. 8.
Closing Remarks – Recap of decisions made, action items, and plans for the next meeting.
None 9.
Adjournment - the meeting adjourned at 11:58 am. 3
